summary: Risk-off Monday: US stocks tumbled as Nvidia led another tech sell-off after Washington tightened AI chip export rules and analysts cut targets; the yen led as a safe haven and the Aussie sank. Nvidia reports Wed 8am Sydney and US retail sales land Wed 12:30am, so tech calls are low conviction. Forex Factory and the Trump feed were unreadable this run; COT on file is dated 3 Nov.
events_next_24h: Tue 11:30 AUD RBA meeting minutes (time unverified)
Wed 08:00 USD Nvidia Q3 earnings (after US close)
tier1_next_14d: FOMC minutes (27-28 Oct meeting) · Thu, 19 Nov, 6:00am
US PCE and personal income (Oct) + Q3 GDP 2nd estimate · Thu, 26 Nov, 12:30am

NQ.why: Tech rout resumed Monday as Nvidia sank on tighter US AI-chip curbs and target cuts; funds 98th-pct long leaves room to unwind.
NQ.risk: Nvidia results Wed 8am Sydney beat and reassure the AI trade.

ES.why: Broad risk-off led by tech with yields still near 5% on Fed hike bets; fund positioning neutral (35th pct).
ES.risk: Strong retail sales with calm yields, or a reassuring Nvidia report.

YM.why: The Dow has held up better as money rotates out of chips, but a broad sell-off drags it too; no positioning data.
YM.risk: Rotation into value accelerates (bullish) or selling broadens (bearish).

RTY.why: High yields weigh on small caps, but I couldn't confirm Monday's Russell move or positioning, so no call.
RTY.risk: A sharp drop in yields after retail sales.

NKD.why: AI and chip selling in the US spills into Japan's chip-heavy index and a firmer yen hurts exporters; funds neutral (46th pct).
NKD.risk: Nvidia beat sparks a chip rebound in Tokyo.

6E.why: Fed hike bets favour the dollar, but I couldn't confirm Monday's euro move; no positioning data on file.
6E.risk: Hot US retail sales lifts the dollar further.

6J.why: Yen led the safe-haven bid on the tech sell-off with USD/JPY pinned near 160 under intervention threat; funds lean long yen (77th).
6J.risk: Strong US data pushes USD/JPY through 160 without Japan acting.

6B.why: Dollar strength leans against sterling, but UK CPI and jobs this week can change the picture; no positioning data.
6B.risk: UK data surprise in either direction.

6A.why: The Aussie sank as the AI sell-off spread; it trades as a risk-on currency. RBA minutes today; no positioning data.
6A.risk: Hawkish RBA minutes or a risk rebound after Nvidia.

ZN.why: Treasuries got only a small safe-haven bid while Fed hike bets keep yields near 5%; retail sales tonight can swing it.
ZN.risk: Weak retail sales rallies bonds; hot sales sinks them.

GC.why: Gold hit its lowest in over a year on Monday despite risk-off, hurt by high yields and Fed hike bets; funds lean short (21st), not crowded.
GC.risk: Middle East escalation or a sharp yield drop triggers short covering.

CL.why: Oil held steady despite renewed Middle East attacks as surplus worries offset; funds crowded short (10th pct) raise squeeze risk.
CL.risk: A confirmed Hormuz supply disruption (bullish) or Iran de-escalation (bearish).
